monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — evidenced by faster paces, elevated HR, and improved aerobic TE and cadence despite lower total km.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved from 13.42 to 13.8 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift across all metrics — indicating better oxygen utilization at given heart rates.

goal_tracker.message: You need 8.3 more km across 3 remaining sessions (e.g., three 2.8–3.0 km runs) to match last month’s volume — achievable without compromising recovery or intensity.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.8 m/sec per bpm while average HR increased +7 bpm — meaning you’re moving faster per unit of cardiac effort, a hallmark of improved cardiovascular fitness.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity work
insights.body: Zone 3+ time jumped from 22% (Z3:19%, Z4:3%, Z5:0%) in May to 45% (Z3:27%, Z4:16%, Z5:2%) in June — reflecting intentional progression but with minimal Z1 recovery work (down from 36% to 20%).

insights.title: Cadence and ground contact time divergence
insights.body: Cadence increased +6 spm (146→152), yet ground contact time remained stable (~312–317 ms) — suggesting strides are shorter but quicker, especially evident in long runs (stride length: 69.5–69.7 cm vs. 91.1 cm in faster 3km run), possibly indicating pacing strategy or fatigue management.

insights.title: High-quality long runs driving TE
insights.body: Two 11 km runs (June 7 & 16) delivered aerobic TE of 3.4 and 3.6 — significantly above your monthly average (2.7) and last month’s best (3.4), confirming effective stimulus for endurance adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) before June 25 to restore Z1/Z2 balance — target pace ~9:00–9:30 min/km based on recent easy-run HR response.
recommendations.reason: Z1 dropped from 36% to 20% and Z2 decreased from 43% to 34%, increasing risk of residual fatigue; your June 4 second run (9:32 min/km @ 137 bpm) shows you can comfortably hold Z2 at that pace.

recommendations.action: Perform one 3 km tempo run at 6:30–6:45 min/km (390–405 sec/km) targeting HR 155–160 bpm, using your June 11 run (6:32 min/km @ 144 bpm) as a baseline for pace readiness.
recommendations.reason: Your best pace improved to 392 sec/km, yet Z4 contribution remains low (16%); this bridges the gap between current Z3 work and race-pace specificity without overreaching.

recommendations.action: Add 3x 30-second barefoot strides post-run (after any session ≥5 km) focusing on light footstrike and cadence ≥165 spm — mirroring your fastest cadence (162 spm on June 11) and reducing vertical oscillation (<8.0 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation averaged 7.7–9.2 cm; lowering it supports efficiency gains, and your stride length variability (69.5–94.7 cm) suggests opportunity to reinforce neuromuscular coordination at speed.

weekly_focus.description: Reintroduce foundational aerobic volume while sharpening form cues — prioritizing HR-controlled ease, controlled tempo, and movement quality to consolidate recent efficiency gains and prevent intensity creep.
suggested_sessions: 6 km progressive run (last 2 km at 7:30 min/km + cadence focus)
